review.summary: Fix for Unitful.jl issue #647, where `uconvert` silently returned NaN, Inf, or 0.0 for units raised to large powers because `basefactor` computed `inex^p` separately for source and target units, letting intermediate floating point factors overflow/underflow before they could cancel. The fix restructures `convfact` to divide the units first (`absoluteunit(FreeUnits(t()))/absoluteunit(FreeUnits(s()))`) and take the base factor of the quotient, so canceling factors never materialize. A secondary `fp_overflow_underflow` guard converts genuinely unrepresentable conversion factors from silent NaN into an ArgumentError.
review.evidence: Issue #647 gives concrete reproducers with wrong numeric output (`uconvert(u"kb"^11, 1.0*u"kb"^12*u"b"^-1)` -> `0.0 kb^11`, `^13` case -> `NaN`), which is a violation of existing documented conversion semantics rather than a missing capability. PR #648 ("Divide units instead of basefactors in convfact()") states "This fixes #647" and matches the diff exactly: convfact now computes a single `conv_units` quotient and calls `basefactor`/`tensfactor` on it. Runtime evidence reports strict_differential=stable_differential over 3 repetitions with the full suite passing on the fixed revision, and test/runtests.jl is touched. Minimization kept 5 of 6 hunks with all_hunks_necessary=true and globally_minimal=true; the dropped hunk is cosmetic (`dpow(x,p)` spacing).

The test diff itself was not provided, only the file path. PR number is null in metadata, though issue_records make the linkage clear.
review.validation_risks: Part of the change adds new ArgumentError throws for true overflow cases (e.g. `uconvert(u"kb^12", 1u"b^12")`), so tests asserting the old NaN behavior would flip to a throw; the PR author acknowledges this as an intentional behavior change. `convfact` is a `@generated` function, so failures surface at compile/specialization time and error messages may be wrapped, which can complicate exact-exception matching in triggers. Floating point equality on conversion factors could be mildly platform sensitive, and the added `absoluteunit(FreeUnits(...))` path touches Affine/ContextUnits handling, so regressions there would be broader than the reported defect.
review.suggested_tests: Assert `uconvert(u"kb"^11, 1.0*u"kb"^12*u"b"^-1) == 1000.0*u"kb"^11` and the `^12`/`^13` variants return finite correct values rather than 0.0/NaN; same for the `kOe^162`/`kOe^163` cases from the issue. Assert `convfact` results are finite and exactly reciprocal for swapped argument order at large exponents. Assert `@test_throws ArgumentError uconvert(u"kb^12", 1u"b^12")` for the genuinely-overflowing factor. Add regression checks that affine units (degC/degF) and ContextUnits still convert correctly through the new `absoluteunit(FreeUnits(...))` path, and that mismatched dimensions still raise DimensionError.

swe.problem_statement:
Converting large powers of units can result in `NaN`, `Inf`, or 0
```julia
julia> using Unitful

julia> uconvert(u"kb"^10, 1.0 * u"kb"^11 * u"b"^-1)
999.9999999999999 kb^10

julia> uconvert(u"kb"^11, 1.0 * u"kb"^12 * u"b"^-1)
0.0 kb^11

julia> uconvert(u"kb"^12, 1.0 * u"kb"^13 * u"b"^-1)
NaN kb^12

julia> uconvert(u"kOe"^161, 1.0 * u"kOe"^162 * u"Oe"^-1)
1000.0 kOe^161

julia> uconvert(u"kOe"^162, 1.0 * u"kOe"^163 * u"Oe"^-1)
Inf kOe^162

julia> uconvert(u"kOe"^163, 1.0 * u"kOe"^164 * u"Oe"^-1)
NaN kOe^163
```

Apologies for the contrived examples, but this is only an issue for units with an “inexact” conversion part `!= 1.0`, and becomes more serious the more different it is from 1. Originally, I ran into this in the context of astrophysical units (see JuliaAstro/UnitfulAstro.jl#33), but I wanted to give a more minimal example with “built-in” units.

The issue is that `inex^p` in `basefactor()`:

https://github.com/PainterQubits/Unitful.jl/blob/bd09747409496a10ec7fab9d719f0841d8f7d5c5/src/units.jl#L229-L247

can result in `Inf` (`inex > 1`) or `0.0` (`inex < 1`) for large `p`, even though all the large factors end up canceling in the conversion. Ideally, `uconvert()` would be smarter and avoid dividing these canceling huge/tiny factors, but at a bare minimum, this should give an error instead of silently returning something wrong!

swe.pr_description:
This fixes #647.

In addition to the change in `convfact()` which allows the examples in #647 to work, I also added an error condition in case of floating point overflow or underflow in `basefactor()`. The latter is not actually needed for these cases anymore, but would still show up when the *real* conversion factor is actually very large/small, such as
```julia
uconvert(u"kb^12", 1u"b^12")
# before:       NaN kb^12
# with this PR: throws ArgumentError
```
Since the current result of `NaN` is just wrong, I’d consider this a bugfix (so the change in behavior is OK), and either way this is an obscure edge case which nobody else seems to have run into so far.
